questions.question: For an inferior good, demand falls when _______.
questions.solution:
• **Inferior good**, in economics, is the good for which **demand decreases when the consumer income rises**, and demand increases when the consumer income decreases.
 
• In the case of normal goods, exactly the opposite is observed.

questions.question: The 'noble tradition' was related to which of the following the dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sen.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'noble tradition**' was related to the **Sen/Sena dynasty**.
 
• The Sena dynasty was a **Hindu dynasty** of the Indian subcontinent in the late classical period.
 
• It **ruled Bengal** in the **11th** and **12th centuries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Rashtrakuta Dynasty:

 
• Between the eighth and the tenth century CE, they ruled parts of South India.
 
• They controlled the entire modern state of Karnataka as well as parts of the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.
 
• They were originally known as the feudatories of the Western Chalukyas of Vatapi.
 
• The Rashtrakuta dynasty was founded by Dhantidurga, who defeated the Chalukyas of Badami.
 
• The Rashtrakutas were known for their worship of Shiva and Vishnu.
 
• Taila II, a feudatory of Krisha III, overthrew the Rashtrakuta dynasty in 973 CE.
 
• Tailpa II was a descendant of the old Chalukya empire.
 
• The Chalukyas of Kalyani was later founded by Taipa II.

Pratihara dynasty:

 
• Pratihara dynasty was founded by King Harichandra at Mandore, a city near Jodhpur in 640 AD. Hence statement 4 is correct.
 
• King Nagbhatta I, who was fourth in line from Harishchandra, captured an area of Bhinmal, which used to be the capital of Gurjara. He earned the title of Gurjeshwar.
 
• This was the beginning of the Imperial Pratihar dynasty which produced great emperors such as Mihir Bhoj I. 
 
• Mihir Bhoj I was the 6th and one of the most powerful emperors of the Imperial Pratihar dynasty who ruled from 836 AD to 885 AD.
 
• He made Kannauj his capital city and extended his empire from the foothills of the Himalayas to the river Narmada in the South and Bengal in the east. 
 
• “Ghaznavid (a Persianate Muslim dynasty of Turkic mamluk origin) invasions weakened the Imperial Pratihars of Kannauj, who we finally defeated by the Rathores or Rashtrakuts.
 
• After the death of the last ruler in the early 11th century, the surviving leadership established the Gwalior Parihar dynasty and the Nagod Parihar dynasty.

Pal Dynasty:

 
• Pala dynasty ruled in Bihar and Bengal from the 8th to the 12th century. 
 
• Its founder was *Gopala*.
 
• His successor was Dharmapala and he greatly expanded the Pala kingdom.
 
• Pala dynasty was a staunch follower of Mahayana and Tantric schools of Buddhism and created the environment for Buddhist monasteries including the *Somapura Mahavihara. *
 
• *Govindapala *was the last ruler of the Pala dynasty.
 
• During the time of Palas, classical Indian philosophy, literature, painting, and sculptures flourished
 
• They also patronized the great universities of *Nalanda and Vikramashila.*

questions.question: What is the purpose of adding Gypsum to the cement?

options.text: To slow down its rate of setting
To increase its rate of setting

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__To slow down its rate of setting.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Gypsum: 

__
 
• Plaster of Paris changes into gypsum on mixing with water and is used for decoration.
 
• Plaster of Paris, commonly called P.O.P. is **Calcium sulphate hemihydrate.**
 
• The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is** CaSO4.1/2 H2O.**
 
• Crystals of gypsum are produced when Plaster of Paris is mixed with water.

 
• **Gypsum** is **calcium sulphate dihydrate** **(CaSO₄.2H₂O)** and a mineral used in cement manufacturing.
 
• It helps in **controlling the rate of hardening of the cement**. A small amount of gypsum is added to the clinker upon its cooling during the final grinding process. It controls the setting of cement.
 
• If it isn’t added, the cement immediately sets post-mixing water and there is no time left for concrete placing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In which of the following countries fascism did originate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Italy__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Fascism is a form of radical authoritarian nationalism that came to prominence in early 20th-century Europe, characterized by one-party totalitarian regimes run by charismatic dictators, glorification of violence, and racist ideology.
 
• The term "fascism" was invented by the Italian Fascist dictator Benito Mussolini (1883 - 1945) and the self-described "philosopher of Fascism" Giovanni Gentile (1875 - 1944).
 
• The Great Depression, which caused significant social unrest throughout the world, led to a major surge of fascism.
 
• Fascism was also popular during the Depression-era outside of Europe, in Japan, Brazil, and Argentina among other nations.
 
• The term originated in Italy and is derived from fascio, meaning a bundle of rods, and is used to symbolize strength through unity: a single rod is easily broken, while the bundle is difficult to break.
 
• After the end of World War I, fascism rose out of relative obscurity into international prominence, with fascist regimes forming most notably in Italy, Germany, and Japan, the three of which would be allied in World War II.​

questions.question:
Along the path of the Vas deferens which glands add their secretions in the sperms?

I. Prostate

II. Seminal vesicles

III. Scrotum
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sperms are transferred from the Vas deferens to the urethra after the collection of secretions from the **Bulbourethral gland**, **Prostate gland**, and **Seminal vesicles**.
 
• These glands provide the semen in bulk.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Prostate gland**

 
 
• The prostate gland is present **below the urinary bladder.**
 
• The prostate gland in males **helps to control urination from the bladder.**
 
• The prostate is a gland** connected to the testicles at one end and the penis at the other end.**
 
• While ejaculating the **prostate stores semen and makes fluid **which liquefies it before it ejects out of the penis.
 
 
 
• **Seminal vesicles**
 
 
• Seminal vesicles secrete** seminal plasma** which helps in **providing nutrition**, and protection and makes** transport easy.**
 
 
 
• **​​Scrotum**
 
 
• The testes are situated outside the abdominal cavity within a pouch called the **scrotum.**
 
• The scrotum **helps in maintaining the low temperature **of the testes (2o – 2.5o C lower than the normal internal body temperature) necessary for** spermatogenesis.**​

questions.question:
Which among the following constituents of the Xylem is/are tubular structure(s)?

I. Tracheids

II. Vessels

III. Xylem fibres
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and II.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• **Xylem** is a kind of tissue in vascular plants which transports nutrients and water from the roots to the leaves.
 
• It is composed of 4 types of cells, which are **tracheids**, **vessels**, **xylem fibres**, and **xylem parenchyma**. Of these, **xylem vessels** and **tracheids** are **tubular structures**.

questions.question: What is the duration of the world’s shortest X-ray laser successfully created by the scientists?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__43 attoseconds__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Scientists from Zurich, Switzerland successfully created the world’s shortest X-ray laser pulse which has a duration of 43 attoseconds.
 
• With the help of this, the researchers can now observe the electron movement in high detail and understand fully the dynamics during a chemical reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen__ discovered X-Rays in 1895.
 
• He discovered this while working with a cathode-ray tube in his laboratory.
 
• X-Ray is an electromagnetic wave of high energy and very short wavelength, which is able to pass through many materials opaque to light.
 
• The frequency of X-Rays is 1016 to 1019 Hz.
 
• X-rays are used to detect cracks in bones, in medicine and industries and also for security purposes.
 
• Soft and Hard X-rays
 
 
• X-rays are usually described by their maximum energy, which is determined by the voltage between the electrodes.
 
• X-rays with high photon energies (above 5–10 keV) are called hard X-rays.
 
• Due to their penetrating ability, hard X-rays are widely used to image the inside of visually opaque objects.
 
• Those with lower energy (and longer wavelength) are called soft X-rays.

questions.question: Terrestrial life forms require _________ water for life processes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fresh.**__

__**Explanation:**__

**Terrestrial life forms** require **fresh water **for life processes such as excretion processes, transportation, and cellular reactions, and not saline water since their bodies cannot get rid of the high amounts of salts present in the saline water.

questions.question: ________ among the following is not a type of JavaScript.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Javascript vbscript.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Javascript vbscript** is not a type of JavaScript.
 
• It is the name of **scripting language**.
 
• Whereas, text/javascript, text/ecmascript and text/vbscript are types of JavaScript.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• JavaScript was originally created to make** web pages more interactive. **
 
• The programs in this language are called **scripts. **
 
• They can be **written in a web page’s HTML and run automatically **as the page loads. 
 
• Scripts are **written and executed as plain text.**
 
• JavaScript **doesn’t need any special compilation** to run. 
 
• JavaScript is **different from Java language.**
